studies.label: Online experiment with professionals: occupation-specific writing with ChatGPT versus Overleaf signup

counts_source.locator: PDF p. 3, Method, first paragraph (recruited count, not an explicit randomized/analyzed participant flow)
counts_source.quote: In a preregistered online experiment, we recruited 453 experienced, college-educated professionals on the survey platform Prolific and assigned each to complete two occupation-specific, incentivized writing tasks (21).

arms.name: Treatment (ChatGPT)
arms.description: After the first writing task, participants were assigned to register for ChatGPT, received guidance, and could use it on the second task (PDF p. 3, Method). Assignment is analyzed, not self-selected actual use.

arms.name: Control (Overleaf signup)
arms.description: Assigned to register for Overleaf to match signup time and hassle, without being told to use it on the second task (PDF p. 3, Method). This is the no-assigned-AI comparison; the paper reports some control-group ChatGPT use (PDF p. 4).

studies.task: Complete occupation-specific professional writing assignments, including press releases, short reports, analysis plans, and delicate emails, before and after the assigned signup intervention.

ai_tool.name: ChatGPT (GPT-3.5)
ai_tool.locator: PDF p. 3, Method, names GPT-3.5 and the experiment dates; PDF p. 1 names ChatGPT. The model release year is not stated.

preregistration.where: AEA RCT Registry: https://www.socialscienceregistry.org/trials/10882; https://doi.org/10.1257/rct.10882-2.1 (PDF p. 11, Data and materials availability).

estimates.outcome: Average evaluator grade: main pooled incentive analysis, Figure 1
estimates.question: with_ai
estimates.measure_detail: Blinded experienced professionals working in the same occupations evaluated workplace writing on a one-to-seven scale; three evaluators saw each output. The saved manuscript does not specify how the average evaluator grade combines the separately named overall, writing-quality, content-quality, and originality grades. Figure 1 uses participant-evaluator observations. Its displayed effect is an adjusted contrast in the pre-to-post change; the arm means are raw post-treatment grades from Panel D.

regression.model: Regression of within-participant post-minus-pre grade change on treatment, occupation*task-order fixed effects, incentive-arm fixed effects, and grader fixed effects, at the participant-evaluator level. Only the coefficient rescaled by the pre-treatment outcome SD is printed; it is recorded in paper_effect. The raw coefficient and its SE are not printed.

paper_effect.standardizer: Pre-treatment standard deviation of the outcome variable (Figure 1 note). The manuscript does not specify the arm composition or whether this SD is across participant means or individual evaluator ratings; it is not identified as the control-arm participant-level SD.

sources.locator: PDF p. 12, Figure 1B, printed effect and interval
sources.quote: Treatment Effect: 0.41 SDs 95% CI: [0.23, 0.59]

sources.locator: PDF p. 12, Figure 1D, printed post-treatment means
sources.quote: Control: Mean 3.802 Treatment: Mean 4.53
terms of pre-treatment standard deviations of the outcome variable.

The coefficients are estimated from regressions of the within-participant change in outcome from pre-to-post treatment on a treatment dummy, occupation*task-order fixed effects, and incentive arm fixed effects.
standard errors are clustered at the person level.

sources.locator: PDF p. 12, Figure 1 note, analysis unit
sources.quote: In Panel (B) this is at the participant-evaluator level,

sources.locator: PDF p. 13, continuation of Figure 1 note
sources.quote: Panel (C) is at the individual level and Panel (D) is at the participant-evaluator level.

sources.locator: PDF p. 12, Figure 1 note, sample restriction
sources.quote: All panels in this figure restrict to the linear and convex incentive groups.
Evaluators were asked to treat the output as if encountered in a work setting and were incentivized to grade outputs carefully on a scale of 1-7 (22).

estimates.notes: Retained as the paper's main pooled treatment comparison across its two main incentive schemes, as mapped in the reconciled screening form. This is not the entire recruited sample: the fixed-time incentive group is excluded. The restriction is explicit and must be retained in any presentation or pooling decision. The confidence interval belongs to the rescaled adjusted coefficient, not to either raw mean or their unadjusted difference. All displayed numbers are printed labels, not values estimated from plotted positions. The plotted arm confidence intervals have no numeric endpoint labels and are not transcribed. No grade SD, raw treatment coefficient, coefficient SE, exact analysis count, or p-value for this figure is printed. The separate narrative and abstract records are overlapping reports of this study, not independent evidence.

not_extracted.what: Average evaluator grade within the fixed-time incentive subgroup
not_extracted.reason: Subgroup contrast excluded by extraction-spec rule 5. PDF p. 4, Productivity: "In this arm, the treatment increased grades by a similar albeit not statistically significant 0.33 standard deviations (26)." PDF p. 10, note 26, says the interval includes zero, but supplies no endpoints or analysis specification.

not_extracted.what: Separate linear versus convex incentive-scheme results
not_extracted.reason: Incentive-cell/subgroup results, not additional full-sample contrasts. PDF p. 4, Productivity, describes the results as virtually identical; no separate grade estimates are printed. The pooled main Figure 1 contrast is retained with its restriction documented.

PDF pp. 4-5 and Figure 2 (PDF pp. 13-15) compare effects over the initial-grade distribution and estimate treatment-by-baseline-grade interactions. These are moderation results, not the requested full-sample treatment effect or similarity across people's outputs.

not_extracted.what: Baseline Average Grade (Task 1) and other Table 1 descriptive comparisons
not_extracted.reason: PDF pp. 18-19, Table 1: these are pre-intervention descriptive/balance statistics. They do not answer with_ai, across_people, or after_ai, and their counts do not establish the post-treatment analysis sample.

not_extracted.what: Grades of raw ChatGPT output versus treated participants who used ChatGPT
not_extracted.reason: PDF p. 5, Human-Machine Interactions: one comparison condition contains raw model output with no person working; the treated-user group is also selected by post-assignment use. It is not an eligible randomized contrast between human assistance arms.

not_extracted.what: Association between editing activity and evaluator grades
not_extracted.reason: PDF p. 5, Human-Machine Interactions: observational association conditional on post-treatment editing behavior, not a randomized assistance effect.

not_extracted.what: Self-reported time taken and objective time/activity measures
not_extracted.reason: PDF pp. 3-5 and Figure 1A/C (PDF pp. 12-13): task duration and activity are process/productivity measures rather than creativity or other characteristics scored on the produced output.
PDF pp. 5-6 and Figure 3A (PDF p. 15): self-reported subjective response, not an output-scored outcome.
Figure 3B and its notes (PDF pp. 15-16): self-reported subjective response, not an output-scored outcome.

not_extracted.what: Concern about worker replacement by AI
not_extracted.reason: PDF pp. 5-6 and Figure 3C with its notes (PDF pp. 15-16): belief/attitude outcome, not scored on creative output.

not_extracted.what: Excitement about AI enhancing worker productivity
not_extracted.reason: PDF pp. 5-6 and Figure 3C with its notes (PDF pp. 15-16): belief/attitude outcome, not scored on creative output.

not_extracted.what: Overall optimism about future advances in AI
not_extracted.reason: PDF pp. 5-6 and Figure 3C with its notes (PDF pp. 15-17): belief/attitude outcome, not scored on creative output.

not_extracted.what: ChatGPT familiarity, registration, task use, continued use at follow-up, and reasons for nonuse
not_extracted.reason: PDF pp. 4-6: adoption, compliance, prior experience, and self-reported use outcomes. The follow-up surveys do not score new unassisted creative outputs and do not supply after_ai estimates.
PDF pp. 4 and 6: ratings of the tool by its users are self-reports, not usefulness/quality scores on the produced work.

not_extracted.what: Optional editing or replacement of the initial response using ChatGPT
not_extracted.reason: PDF p. 4, final paragraph: the additional opportunity in a subset of treated participants reports choices to edit or replace output, without an output-quality contrast against a randomized comparison arm.
PDF p. 3, Method, reports an average within-essay cross-evaluator correlation of 0.44; PDF p. 10, note 23, defines it. This is rating reliability, not a treatment-control effect.

open_items: Exact participant counts randomized and analyzed, overall and by assigned arm and outcome, are not explicitly printed. The recruitment count and Table 1 descriptive/baseline counts cannot resolve the post-treatment analysis Ns. No counts were inferred from proportions or degrees of freedom.

Figure 1 excludes the fixed-time incentive group and pools the linear and convex incentive groups. It is retained as the paper's designated main pooled analysis; its restricted scope should be reviewed explicitly under the extraction full-sample rule.
The saved manuscript does not reconcile the narrative standardized average-grade result with Figure 1, or identify the exact sample and model behind the narrative result and abstract percentage.

No participant-level or rating-level grade SD, raw grade-change coefficient, or coefficient SE is printed. The precise population and observation level used for the Figure 1 pre-treatment SD are not specified.

Separate numerical results, scoring rubrics, analysis units, models, and sample counts for originality, overall grade, writing quality, and content quality are absent. The aggregation relating these grades to average evaluator grade is not defined.

Supplementary Materials are referenced but not embedded in the saved PDF; supplement-manifest.json lists no saved supplementary files for this paper. Referenced Lee bounds, baseline-covariate robustness, separate grade results, and compliance-adjusted estimates cannot be checked against a saved supplement.
The saved manuscript confirms preregistration but does not specify which grade was the preregistered primary outcome. Participant country and the AI model's release year are not stated.
notes: Read all PDF pages and the complete markdown conversion, including references, figure notes, Table 1, and the closing table notes. Inspected the figures and descriptive table before the design text; recovered Table 1 with pymupdf.find_tables(). All recorded estimate numbers were confirmed in PDF text. The study randomizes assistance between people and measures tasks before and after treatment; it is not a randomized-order crossover, so within_person is null. Professional output quality and its component grades follow the screening form's usefulness classification; originality is novelty. The manuscript has no across_people or after_ai output outcome. The average-grade figure, narrative, and abstract estimates are overlapping representations, not independent samples, and must not all enter a pooled estimate. Qualitatively reported grade contrasts remain present with null statistics. The screening form reports no stated shared sample; shared_sample is null. No posted-data calculation or result reconstruction was performed. Only the authorized extraction JSON was written.
